resyncToken.description: A single-use waiver on a canonical_merge resync, bound to this stream's filters and the account. Send it as the resyncToken query parameter on a snapshot whose filters are the same as, or narrower than, this stream. info.description:
Australian racing odds, prices, and results.

All endpoints are relative to this document's server URL and require an API key
in the `X-API-Key` header. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents carrying a
stable `code` you can branch on. Collections are cursor-paginated:
follow `next` rather than constructing page parameters.

For `GET /events/snapshot`, the first request supplies the scope and
each later page request supplies only its `after` or `before`
cursor. That sealed cursor preserves the resolved time window and stream
boundary; do not repeat filters or a limit on later pages.

The intended workflow is snapshot, then follow: take current prices for the
races you care about with `GET /events/snapshot` (or one race with
`GET /events/{id}/snapshot`), then connect `GET /stream`
with `snapshot=none` and the continuation's exact filters and `cursor`.
Apply ordered frames until the following `sync` frame before treating
the REST baseline as reconciled. Each odds
row names `key` (`win` or `place`) so you can
render a race card without joining a market collection. Stream frames are
unmetered, so following is cheaper and faster than polling.

Empty collections are always `[]`, never `null`.

New fields and new endpoints can appear without a new version. Ignore fields
you do not recognise.

get.description:
Current field, prices, and coverage for a page of races matching your filters — plus the `stream` handoff to follow them live.

The first request declares the scope. Each later page sends only the opaque `after` or `before` token returned by the prior page; it restores the sealed scope and returns the same `stream.cursor`, captured before the first page was read. Paging to the end and then following cannot miss a change to a race you read earlier.

A `resyncToken` from a canonical_merge resync frame waives this snapshot, including extra units, when it is valid for the account and these filters are the same as or narrower than the stream that issued it. A wider snapshot is charged normally. It is single-use and expires after a few minutes. A missing, reused, expired, other-account, or over-quota token is charged normally.

get.description:
A resumable stream of everything changing in the races you filter for.

Start with a REST snapshot — `GET /events/snapshot` for a page of races, or `GET /events/{id}/snapshot` for one race — then connect with `snapshot=none` and the `cursor` that response returned. That is the fast, resumable path and the one to build on.

`snapshot=full` streams the current state as idless frames before going live, so one connection needs no REST call. It requires an `event`, `meeting`, or `venue` filter: on a broader set of races it takes minutes and starts over on any drop, so it is refused. The `sync` frame commits the snapshot and carries its first resumable SSE id.

After `sync`, reconnect with the latest SSE id in `Last-Event-ID` (or the `cursor` parameter). Before `sync`, discard a partial full snapshot and start it again without a cursor. Within one race, a price frame always arrives before the coverage frame whose `book` it completed, so the first coverage frame with `book.status` `full` means you already hold every price in that book. On a `resync` frame, snapshot again over REST (or follow `stream.url` from the new snapshot) and reconnect with the cursor that response returned. Trainer, rider, and owner merges never resync a stream; they arrive as entrant frames. A canonical_merge resync frame may carry `resyncToken`. Pass it as the `resyncToken` query parameter on `GET /events/snapshot` or `GET /events/{id}/snapshot` when that snapshot's filters are the same as, or narrower than, this stream. On a single-race snapshot the path id and source are the only filters that count, and any other filter parameter is charged. The matching snapshot is not charged, including its extra units. A wider snapshot is charged normally. The token is single-use, bound to the account and these filters, and expires after a few minutes. A replay of the same control does not mint another. A missing, reused, expired, other-account, or over-quota token is charged normally. Frames are not metered.
